items.title: Danny Barker — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: You never see Clarence [Williams], but you heard of him.

ctx.x: Those things that Sidney Bechet recorded with Clarence Williams in ’23 . . .

It was Clarence Williams. It wasn’t Sidney Bechet. It was mostly, they were accompanying singers. That’s what Clarence Williams was great for. All these dozens of singers that the companies would get him to record with them, because he’s from the South, he knew how to record, and he was, other than that, he was a businessman. Clarence Williams would get to those people and they would listen to what he said, because he had a foresight and he was a brilliant man, and he was a great composer. He wrote some great…
You saw a lot of people here, musicians . . .
